origin.description: The direct sum of two numeric vectors or matrices, returned as a block diagonal matrix.
origin.details: A vector is converted to a one-column matrix. The result is the block diagonal matrix with x in the upper left and y in the lower right.
origin.example: x <- matrix(seq(1, 4)); y <- matrix(seq(5, 8)); print(x %s% y)

translation.description: The direct sum of two numeric vectors or matrices, returned as a block diagonal matrix.
translation.details: A vector is converted to a one-column matrix. The result is the block diagonal matrix with x in the upper left and y in the lower right.
translation.example:
from matrixcalc.s_op import s_op
import numpy as np
x = np.arange(1, 5, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 1)
y = np.arange(5, 9, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 1)
print(s_op(x, y))
